claims.explanation: Atorvastatin's selective anticancer activity is most plausibly driven by HMGCR (the mevalonate pathway) dependency: lines with high HMGCR/mevalonate-pathway expression and intact sterol-feedback signaling are sensitized, while lines with low pathway flux or mutations that bypass the mevalonate requirement (e.g., TP53 loss, PTEN loss with high AKT/mTOR-driven sterol synthesis) are relatively protected. The virtual-cell signature (HMGCR induction, lovastatin/rosuvastatin/fluvastatin as top matches) confirms on-target HMGCR inhibition as the mechanism, so selectivity should track with mevalonate-pathway gene expression and cholesterol-auxotrophy markers rather than with any single lineage.

High LDLR permits cholesterol uptake from serum, reducing dependence on de novo mevalonate synthesis
Master regulator of sterol biosynthesis; active SREBP2 indicates high mevalonate-pathway flux
Cholesterol efflux capacity can buffer intracellular sterol depletion caused by HMGCR inhibition
p53 loss allows survival under metabolic stress and reduces statin-induced apoptosis
PTEN loss with hyperactive PI3K/AKT/mTOR increases sterol demand and mevalonate dependency
Oncogenic KRAS requires mevalonate-derived geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate for membrane localization
Annotated atorvastatin target; AHR signaling intersects with cholesterol metabolism and drug response
Annotated atorvastatin target; DPP4 activity may modulate metabolic stress responses
Major atorvastatin-metabolizing enzyme; high expression lowers effective intracellular drug exposure
AP-1 stress response induced by atorvastatin in the virtual cell, marking responsive lines
Proliferation marker downregulated by atorvastatin; high baseline PCNA may indicate resistant, rapidly cycling lines
